Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for acute progressive upper lip swelling and breathing difficulty after prawn soup; clinician suspected anaphylaxis, activated emergency response, advised antihistamine while awaiting ambulance, and arranged post-hospital follow-up for epinephrine auto-injector.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling of upper lip with difficulty breathing and dizziness after eating prawn soup.
- Timeline:
  - ~19:00: Ate prawn soup (first time trying prawn at usual venue).
  - ~30 minutes later: Noticed lip tingling/swelling at left corner first, then upper lip; progressive worsening.
  - During call: Ongoing swelling “getting bigger,” sensation of difficulty breathing; patient unsure if chest is tight; reports dizziness.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None reported.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Upper lip swelling, dyspnea (“can’t breathe that well”), dizziness.
  - Uncertain: Chest tightness.
  - No other associated symptoms documented (no rash, wheeze, GI symptoms mentioned).
- Relevant prior episode: Approximately 1 year ago after late-night Chinese meal (patient was intoxicated); woke next morning “quite swollen” with difficult breathing; treatment details unclear.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives/uncertainties as documented): No explicit documentation of hives, wheeze, stridor, GI upset, syncope.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma: Uses salbutamol inhaler regularly (dose/route/frequency not documented). No controller inhaler reported. No recent exacerbation data provided.
- Peanut allergy: Longstanding. History of severe reaction in childhood requiring hospital visit per patient recollection; patient unsure if epinephrine injection was used.
- No other conditions documented.

Social History:
- Alcohol: Reports being “quite drunk” during prior episode a year ago; no routine use frequency documented.
- Living situation: Alone at time of call; mother arrived during call to assist.
- Tobacco and other substances: Not documented.
- Occupation/finances: Not documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam: Not performed (telemedicine). Patient-reported findings: progressive upper lip swelling; difficulty breathing; dizziness.

Investigations:
- None performed or reported during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute allergic reaction with concern for anaphylaxis after prawn ingestion
  - Assessment: Rapid-onset, progressive lip swelling (~30 min post-ingestion), dyspnea, and dizziness following prawn soup; prior similar reaction history; peanut allergy history. High concern for anaphylaxis.
  - Plan:
    - Emergency services: Advised immediate activation of 999 for suspected anaphylaxis and urgent hospital evaluation.
    - Interim measures: Advised to take available antihistamines while awaiting ambulance (specific agent/dose/route not documented).
    - Safety: Ensure constant supervision; mother present to call 999 and stay with patient.
    - Follow-up: After hospital discharge, instructed to contact clinic to arrange epinephrine auto-injector (“injections and things”) and further management.
- Issue 2: Asthma (baseline condition)
  - Assessment: Uses salbutamol inhaler regularly; no controller inhaler reported.
  - Plan: No acute changes discussed during this consult.
- Issue 3: Peanut allergy with prior severe reaction in childhood
  - Assessment: History suggests severe reaction requiring hospital care at ~age 6; patient unsure about prior epinephrine use.
  - Plan: Post-hospital follow-up to arrange epinephrine auto-injector as above.

General plan items:
- Patient advised to return call to clinic after hospital care for further allergy management and prescriptions.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; comprehensive ROS; physical exam; complete allergy list beyond peanut; current medication list with doses/frequencies; past surgical history; family history; smoking/substance history; detailed anaphylaxis action plan not discussed; documentation of actual antihistamine taken (agent/dose/time) not recorded.
- Internal conflicts: Initial note mentioned “sandwich,” patient clarified it was prawn soup (conflict noted, resolved by patient clarification). Patient uncertain about presence of chest tightness.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses/inaudible fragments; urgent situation limited detail collection.
